desc:
The array bits contains only 0 and 1. Cut it at one position into two non-empty contiguous parts, a left part and a right part. The score of the cut is the number of 0s in the left part plus the number of 1s in the right part.

Return the largest score over all possible cuts.

bits = [0, 1, 1, 0, 1]
cut after index 0: left [0] has 1 zero, right [1,1,0,1] has 3 ones -> 4
cut after index 3: left [0,1,1,0] has 2 zeros, right [1] has 1 one -> 3
answer = 4
hints: There are only n - 1 cut positions. Counting zeros and ones for each cut from scratch is O(n) each; how can neighbouring cuts share work?
Moving the cut one step to the right moves a single element from the right part to the left part. How does the score change if that element is a 0? If it is a 1?

Start with the total number of ones as the 'right ones'. Sweep the cut from left to right: a moved 0 adds one to the zeros on the left, a moved 1 removes one from the ones on the right. Track the best score over the n - 1 valid cuts.
editorial: Let zerosLeft be the zeros in the left part and onesRight the ones in the right part. Start with an empty left part: zerosLeft = 0 and onesRight = total ones. Extend the left part one element at a time: a 0 increases zerosLeft, a 1 decreases onesRight. After each extension (but only while the right part is still non-empty) evaluate zerosLeft + onesRight and keep the maximum.

Equivalently, the score is zeros(prefix) + (ones_total - ones(prefix)), a prefix-sum expression. The sweep runs in O(n) time with O(1) memory. Mind the non-empty rule: the cut after the last element is not allowed, so the loop stops one element early.
